Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(\varphi\) be Euler’s totient function, with \(\varphi(1)=1\).

First, the condition forces a very rigid structure.

From \(i=j\), we have
\[
|A_i|=i.
\]
If \(d\mid i\), then
\[
|A_d\cap A_i|=\gcd(d,i)=d=|A_d|,
\]
so
\[
A_d\subseteq A_i.
\]
Therefore, if \(g=\gcd(i,j)\), then
\[
A_g\subseteq A_i\cap A_j.
\]
But both sets have size \(g\), so in fact
\[
A_i\cap A_j=A_g. \tag{1}
\]

Now consider any element \(x\) that appears in at least one \(A_i\), and let
\[
m(x)=\min\{i:x\in A_i\}.
\]
If \(m(x)\mid n\), then \(x\in A_{m(x)}\subseteq A_n\). Conversely, if \(x\in A_n\) but \(m(x)\nmid n\), let \(g=\gcd(m(x),n)<m(x)\). By (1),
\[
x\in A_{m(x)}\cap A_n=A_g,
\]
contradicting the minimality of \(m(x)\). Hence
\[
x\in A_n \iff m(x)\mid n.
\]

Let \(f(n)\) be the number of elements whose first-appearance index is \(n\). Then
\[
|A_n|=\sum_{d\mid n} f(d)=n.
\]
Since
\[
\sum_{d\mid n}\varphi(d)=n,
\]
Möbius inversion gives \(f(n)=\varphi(n)\). Thus, up to naming the elements, the sequence is forced: for each \(n\), there are \(\varphi(n)\) “type-\(n\)” elements, and a type-\(n\) element lies in \(A_m\) exactly when \(n\mid m\).

Now restrict to divisors of \(250=2\cdot 5^3\). For \(b=0,1,2,3\), define
\[
s_b=\varphi(5^b)=\varphi(2\cdot 5^b).
\]
Thus
\[
(s_0,s_1,s_2,s_3)=(1,4,20,100).
\]
Let \(O_b\) be the type-\(5^b\) elements, and \(E_b\) the type-\(2\cdot 5^b\) elements; each has size \(s_b\).

For any labeling by positive integers, set
\[
X_b=\max\{\text{labels in }O_0\cup\cdots\cup O_b\},
\]
\[
Y_b=\max\{\text{labels in }E_0\cup\cdots\cup E_b\}.
\]
Then
\[
\max A_{5^b}=X_b,\qquad \max A_{2\cdot 5^b}=\max(X_b,Y_b).
\]
So the desired sum is
\[
S=\sum_{b=0}^3\bigl(X_b+\max(X_b,Y_b)\bigr).
\]

Since \(X_b\) and \(Y_b\) are nondecreasing, and if \(X_b\le t\) then all elements of \(O_0,\dots,O_b\) have labels \(\le t\) (and similarly for \(Y_b\)), we have for every integer \(t\):
\[
\sum_{b:X_b\le t}s_b+\sum_{b:Y_b\le t}s_b\le t. \tag{2}
\]

Now sort the eight numbers
\[
X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3,Y_0,Y_1,Y_2,Y_3
\]
as
\[
t_1\le t_2\le \cdots \le t_8.
\]
Attach to \(X_b\) and \(Y_b\) the size \(s_b\), and let \(p_i\) be the attached size for \(t_i\). The first \(i\) sorted values are all \(\le t_i\), so by (2),
\[
p_1+\cdots+p_i\le t_i.
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{i=1}^8 t_i\ge \sum_{i=1}^8 (p_1+\cdots+p_i).
\]
The multiset of the \(p_i\) is
\[
\{1,1,4,4,20,20,100,100\}.
\]
The minimum possible sum of prefix sums occurs when they are in increasing order:
\[
1,\ 2,\ 6,\ 10,\ 30,\ 50,\ 150,\ 250.
\]
Hence
\[
\sum_{i=1}^8 t_i\ge 1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250=499.
\]
Finally,
\[
S=\sum_{b=0}^3\bigl(X_b+\max(X_b,Y_b)\bigr)
\ge \sum_{b=0}^3 (X_b+Y_b)
=\sum_{i=1}^8 t_i
\ge 499.
\]

It remains to show that \(499\) is attainable. Use the forced type model and label the relevant 250 elements as follows:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{type} & \text{labels used} \\
\hline
1 & 1 \\
2 & 2 \\
5 & 3,4,5,6 \\
10 & 7,8,9,10 \\
25 & 11,\dots,30 \\
50 & 31,\dots,50 \\
125 & 51,\dots,150 \\
250 & 151,\dots,250
\end{array}
\]

Assign all other types labels larger than \(250\). Define \(A_n\) to be the set of labels of all types dividing \(n\). Then
\[
|A_i\cap A_j|=\sum_{d\mid \gcd(i,j)}\varphi(d)=\gcd(i,j),
\]
so the sequence is valid.

For the divisors of \(250\), the maxima are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\max A_1&=1,\\
\max A_2&=2,\\
\max A_5&=6,\\
\max A_{10}&=10,\\
\max A_{25}&=30,\\
\max A_{50}&=50,\\
\max A_{125}&=150,\\
\max A_{250}&=250.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their sum is
\[
1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250=499.
\]

Therefore the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}
\]
